cases.name: parallel-divergence
cases.prompt:
Here is an Anchor the user accepted last week. Two agents will now work in parallel: one on the sync engine, one on the web UI. Before delegating, check whether the Anchor is safe to rely on and tell me what, if anything, must change.

# Pause syncing for a playlist
## Intended outcome
Users can pause a playlist so the nightly sync stops changing it, and resume it later.
## Observable success
- A paused playlist is not modified by the nightly sync.
- The user can resume a paused playlist.
## Sources and acceptance
Accepted by user in chat, 2026-11-04.
cases.trap: Declaring the Anchor complete because it has outcome, success and acceptance sections, or inventing technical rules instead of naming the user-owned semantic gap.
expectations: Identifies that behaviour on resume is undefined (e.g. whether videos published during the pause are backfilled or skipped)
Explains that the two agents could implement incompatible meanings while both following the Anchor
Frames the gap as a decision for the user (asks or records an open question) rather than silently picking an answer
Does not treat the existing acceptance record as covering the newly resolved behaviour
negative_expectations: States the Anchor is ready for delegation as-is
Adds a resume/backfill rule to the Anchor and marks it accepted without user confirmation

cases.name: no-invented-targets
cases.prompt: Capture a durable Anchor for this request so a separate agent can implement and another can verify it: 'Search in our self-hosted media app is painfully slow on my library of about 40k tracks. Make it feel instant like Spotify's.' No other information is available.
cases.trap: Converting 'feel instant' into a fabricated numeric SLA (e.g. p95 < 100 ms) placed in the success criteria, even if labelled proposed, or prescribing an index/engine.
expectations: Keeps the user's wording or a qualitative observable outcome for speed
Any numeric latency target appears only as an open question for the user to decide, not in the observable success criteria
Leaves the technical approach (indexing, search engine, caching) open
negative_expectations: Places any invented numeric latency figure (e.g. p95, ms) inside Observable success, even if labelled proposed
Mandates a specific technology such as SQLite FTS5, Elasticsearch, or Meilisearch

cases.name: amendment-contradicts-exclusion
cases.prompt:
Existing accepted Anchor excerpt:
## Scope and exclusions
In scope: routing YouTube subscriptions into the user's own Spotify playlists.
Out of scope: writing to any playlist the user does not own (collaborative or followed playlists).
## Sources and acceptance
Accepted by user, 2026-10-02.

New user message today (2026-11-11): 'Can routing also target the collaborative playlist my friends and I share? We use it to swap music.' Update the Anchor accordingly.
cases.trap: Treating it as a minor change covered by prior acceptance and editing scope silently, without noticing it reverses an explicit exclusion, or recording the broadened scope as already accepted.
expectations: Points out that the request reverses an explicit prior exclusion
Has a distinct Decisions/rationale entry recording the new request with date 2026-11-11 and the user's reason (shared with friends)
Updates or replaces the out-of-scope line rather than leaving contradictory statements
Raises any consequential sub-question the user owns (e.g. whether this extends to all collaborative playlists or only that shared one)
negative_expectations: Leaves the old exclusion and new scope both present without reconciliation
Keeps the original 2026-10-02 acceptance as the sole acceptance evidence for the amended scope
Presents the broadened scope as already accepted
